Node 1 (accent) can be sent to any of the four corners by a symmetry, so its coset is 1, 2, 3, 4. With node 1 held in place, node 2 can only stay or swap with its opposite neighbor 4 (both teal), so its coset is 2, 4; after that nodes 3 and 4 are fixed. The card lists the cosets and multiplies their sizes, 4 × 2 × 1 × 1 = 8 symmetries." width="100%"} An automorphism is a relabeling of the nodes that maps the graph onto itself, edge for edge: a symmetry. Taking the nodes in ID order, the coset of a node lists the nodes it can be sent to by an automorphism that leaves every smaller node in place. This compact summary of the symmetry group (a stabilizer chain) answers which nodes are interchangeable, gives the number of symmetries as the product of the coset sizes, and is what `subgraph_isomorphisms(..., symmetry=True)` uses to skip symmetric matches. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node attribute name, or list of names; symmetries must map nodes onto nodes with equal values. [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional edge attribute name, or list of names; symmetries must map edges onto edges with equal values. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : For every node ID, in ID order, the IDs in its coset: the node itself first, then the larger IDs it can be swapped with, in ID order. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For node $v$, a node $u > v$ belongs to the coset when an isomorphism search of the graph onto itself succeeds with every node below $v$ fixed and $v$ sent to $u$ (each enforced by a unique color, which color refinement propagates). The product of the coset sizes is the order of the automorphism group, by the orbit-stabilizer theorem. NetworkX's `ISMAGS.analyze_symmetry()` returns the same cosets for the nodes it reaches, though its partition-based search can miss members (on the Petersen graph it gives `[1, 4]` for node 1 where the coset is `[1, 4, 5]`), so the product there can fall short of the group order. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A square has 8 symmetries: node 1 can go to any corner (4 ways), and with it fixed, node 2 can swap with its opposite neighbor 4 (2 ways): ::: {#adf4731f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(4).automorphism_cosets() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: [1, 2, 3, 4], 2: [2, 4], 3: [3], 4: [4]} ``` ::: :::
